texts: Right bundle branch block is a relatively common result of VSD closure, in about 35 percent of patients: D.
The right bundle runs close to the lower rim of a perimembranous defect, and stitches or a ventriculotomy can interrupt it; the block is usually harmless.
Complete heart block after repair is not always permanent, and operative mortality for isolated VSD is now well under 1 percent.
Transcatheter devices exist for perimembranous defects, though their use is limited by heart block.
In the picture, one of the three patched hotels has the right branch of the crackling bundle snapped.
Memory hook: one patched wall in three snaps the right branch.
